newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber mixed, November up on bull spreading.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber mixed, November up on bull spreading.

text.p: CME lumber futures were mixed Friday, with the November contract higher, underpinned by bull spreading, analysts said.
"They're still buying the November and selling it against the January, March and other back months," one lumber analyst said.
The spreading was spurred in part by expectations for tight deliverable supplies of lumber in November, sources said.
Early weakness in November was linked to profit taking following fresh contract highs earlier this week, analysts said.
Prices were also supported by talk of a strike at one Canadian mill and a slowdown in production at several others, cash sources said.
"This is a market driven by lack of supply more than anything else," one analyst said.
Lumber was trading up $3.00 to down $0.10 with November up $3.00 at $421.20 per tbf. November set a new contract high at $421.20.
